note: Short definitions of every coded category, read by the gold-set coder app and mirrored in CODEBOOK.md section 8. Sources in brackets; 'working definition' marks the seminar's own wording. Terms verdict_*, unassessable_* and crit_* (and rating_notes) belong to the human ratings v1.1.0 (agents/coder/ratings.schema.json) and are taken from agents/advance/RUBRIC.md v1.0.1, sections 4 to 7; CODEBOOK.md does not mirror them.

anomaly.label: anomaly
anomaly.def: A surprising observation that no stated expectation predicted; the work starts by explaining or establishing it [codebook 2; Klahr & Simon 1999].

problem.label: problem
problem.def: An unsolved question the literature names; no surprising observation and no prior hypothesis drives the start [codebook 2].

challenged_result.label: challenged result
challenged_result.def: A published result that the paper sets out to check, test, or replicate [codebook 2].

hypothesis.label: hypothesis
hypothesis.def: A hypothesis, or a theory's prediction, stated before the work and directing it [codebook 2].

data_without_theory.label: data without theory
data_without_theory.def: Data in hand, collected without a guiding question or theory, that the paper mines or describes [codebook 2].

capability.label: capability
capability.def: A new instrument, method, archive, or computer that opens the work; questions come after [codebook 2; Hacking 1983].

external_goal.label: external goal
external_goal.def: A goal set by someone else, such as a benchmark, a mission requirement, or a mandate [codebook 2].

new.label: new
new.def: A step forward in the work [codebook 3].

repeat.label: repeat
repeat.def: The same node as the step just before, with no failure reported [codebook 3].

return_after_failure.label: return after failure
return_after_failure.def: The document says an earlier attempt failed, mismatched, or was revised, and this step goes back to it [codebook 3].

review_forced.label: review forced
review_forced.def: A referee, editor, or commenter asked for it; review sequence only [codebook 3].

declined.label: declined
declined.def: A review request answered in the rebuttal without new work; review sequence only [codebook 3].

inherited.label: inherited
inherited.def: Done in the authors' own earlier work and cited, not performed in this paper [codebook 3].

cited.label: cited
cited.def: A result, expectation, or claim taken from other groups' work and used, not performed here [codebook 3].

kept.label: kept
kept.def: A claim is retained, with a status [codebook 5].

excluded.label: excluded
excluded.def: A rival is rejected and that rejection is the result [codebook 5].

contradicted.label: contradicted
contradicted.def: An earlier published claim is shown wrong; this counts as a success [codebook 5; convenor decision, 2026-10-21].

no_conclusion.label: no conclusion
no_conclusion.def: The work ends without a conclusion; this is failure [codebook 5; convenor decision, 2026-10-21].

confirmed.label: confirmed
confirmed.def: The claim survived a test it could have failed, against stated rivals [decision-tree.qmd; mode page: hypothesis assessment].

best_explanation.label: best explanation
best_explanation.def: The best among the stated rivals, not singled out by a decisive test; typical of trace series [decision-tree.qmd; Cleland 2002].

regularity_in_range.label: regularity in range
regularity_in_range.def: A relation fitted across repeated cases, with the range where it holds stated [decision-tree.qmd; mode page: regularities].

estimate_with_resolution.label: estimate with resolution
estimate_with_resolution.def: A latent quantity inferred with its resolution and uncertainty [decision-tree.qmd; mode page: estimation].

capability_characterized.label: capability characterized
capability_characterized.def: An instrument or method whose performance is characterized: what it can measure or compute, and how well [decision-tree.qmd; mode pages: instruments, methods].

forecast_skill.label: forecast skill
forecast_skill.def: A forecast frozen before the outcome and scored against a reference [mode page: simulation; Charney et al. 1950].

none.label: none
none.def: No claim with a status (use with no conclusion) [codebook 5].

strong_inference.label: strong inference
strong_inference.def: Several rivals share one crucial test whose outcomes differ across them; every outcome excludes at least one; survivors are refined [unit.qmd composition table; Platt 1964, p. 347].

trace_series.label: trace series
trace_series.def: Conditions found, not set; observations repeated over independent traces stand in for varied auxiliaries; the claim is the best explanation within the stated rivals [unit.qmd; Cleland 2002, pp. 484, 487-491].

natures_repetition.label: nature's repetition
natures_repetition.def: Conditions found but repeated by nature; a regularity is fitted across the repetitions, with no power to set or remove the conditions [unit.qmd; Cleland 2002, p. 485].

capability_first.label: capability first
capability_first.def: New capability, then observation, then establishing the phenomenon until it repeats, then the question; no rival exists until that is done [unit.qmd; Kolbl-Ebert 2001; Keeling 1960].

forecast_verification.label: forecast verification
forecast_verification.def: The expectation is frozen by computation before the observation exists; observation and comparison come later, scored against a reference [unit.qmd; Charney et al. 1950, p. 245].

exploration_first.label: exploration first
exploration_first.def: Conditions are varied until a phenomenon is stable before any question or rival is posed (working definition after Steinle 1997).

independent_replication.label: independent replication
independent_replication.def: A published result is re-derived with independent data, methods, or both (working definition after Schmidt 2009, conceptual replication).

none_fits.label: none fits
none_fits.def: No listed composition describes the walk; say why in Limits [codebook 6].

gate_action.label: action gate
gate_action.def: Did a stated hypothesis direct the key data acquisition? yes, no, or partly [codebook 6].

gate_claim.label: claim gate
gate_claim.def: Did the main claim face a test it could have failed? yes, no, or partly [codebook 6].

gate_registration.label: registration gate
gate_registration.def: Was anything (hypothesis, analysis, threshold) fixed before the data were seen? yes, no, or partly [codebook 6].

role_corrective.label: corrective
role_corrective.def: Fixes an error or a wrong belief in prior knowledge (working definition; Scientific Advance Profile v1).

role_enabling.label: enabling
role_enabling.def: Makes new work possible: data, an instrument, a method, a standard (working definition).

role_integrative.label: integrative
role_integrative.def: Connects results, data sets, or fields into one account (working definition).

role_cumulative.label: cumulative
role_cumulative.def: Adds to an established line of work within its frame (working definition).

role_transformative.label: transformative
role_transformative.def: Changes how a problem is framed or approached (working definition).

v_reproduction.label: reproduction
v_reproduction.def: Same data, steps, code and conditions, run again, including rerunning a model on the same input; counts as V partial [NASEM 2019; codebook 3a].

v_replication.label: replication
v_replication.def: New data for the same question: new samples, period, event, independent data set, or held-out data; V full [NASEM 2019].

v_method.label: method
v_method.def: The same data analysed with a different method, model, or code; V full [codebook 3a].

v_robustness.label: robustness
v_robustness.def: Conditions, parameters, auxiliaries, or components deliberately varied: sensitivity tests, ablations, alternative processing; V full [codebook 3a].

v_control.label: control
v_control.def: A control or reference the result is compared against: synthetic tests, blanks, reference stations, null models, baselines; V full [codebook 3a].

v_generalization.label: generalization
v_generalization.def: The result tested in another region, context, population, or task; V full [NASEM 2019].

verdict_achieved.label: achieved
verdict_achieved.def: No unassessable condition holds and at least one gain meets every criterion: M1, M2, W1, W2, W3 and W4 (W3 may be not applicable). The gain you rate is the first such gain, starting with the headline claim. Advance score 2 to 5 [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

verdict_not_demonstrated.label: not demonstrated
verdict_not_demonstrated.def: No unassessable condition holds and every gain in the paper has at least one criterion not met. The gain you rate is the headline gain. Advance score 1. A highly novel claim that is not warranted is not demonstrated; a modest but warranted correction is achieved [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

verdict_unassessable.label: unassessable
verdict_unassessable.def: One of the conditions U1 to U5 holds; name it. No advance score. Unassessable is not a hedge for a hard case: if you can judge, judge, and lower the confidence [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

unassessable_U1.label: U1 incomplete text
unassessable_U1.def: The text is incomplete: only an abstract, missing pages or sections, or unreadable extraction where the results should be [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

unassessable_U2.label: U2 result not in text
unassessable_U2.def: The result every headline component rests on is stated nowhere in the text or captions, only by reference ('see Fig. 4', 'Supplementary Table 2') with no number or direction. A result stated in the text with a pointer to a figure or supplement is evidence: judge it and lower the confidence [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

unassessable_U3.label: U3 starting state unknown
unassessable_U3.def: The starting state cannot be established from the paper and your knowledge, so M1 cannot be judged [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

unassessable_U4.label: U4 not eligible
unassessable_U4.def: Not a primary Earth-science research article (your eligibility answer is no). A screen failure, reported outside the success fraction [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

unassessable_U5.label: U5 other
unassessable_U5.def: Other: name exactly what is missing in the verdict reasons. Use sparingly [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 6].

crit_M1.label: M1 beyond the starting state
crit_M1.def: The gain changes the epistemic state: new content, or a change in the confidence, scope or standing of a known result (a replication of a contested result, a correction). Not met by a restatement of a known result, a result already established by observation, or a prediction already validated at the same place and scale. A first observational confirmation of a theoretical expectation meets M1. Not met when the gap the paper claims is not real (the cited prior work or your knowledge already covers it). When an exact precedent exists, M1 is normally not met unless the gain is a replication or a correction [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 4].

crit_M2.label: M2 meaningful for its gain type
crit_M2.def: Knowledge (a fact, measurement, estimate or observation): changes a specific prior assertion or covers new ground, by a place, period, variable or resolution not previously observed (checked against the cited literature, not the paper's gap statement); a reduced uncertainty stated in magnitude, or an estimate differing from a cited prior value beyond the stated uncertainty; the detection or ruling out of a change or trend; or a constrained parameter or resolved discrepancy. Understanding (a mechanism or explanation): accounts for observations previously unexplained or explained differently, or discriminates between rivals, by a formal test, named alternatives each excluded by a named observation, two or more independent lines of evidence that agree, or a feasibility result under stated, realistic conditions; a story fitted after the fact does not meet M2. Capability (a method, data set, instrument, code or standard): demonstrated on at least one case against an existing alternative, a benchmark, synthetic truth or independent observations, with a reported comparison result showing the improvement; a data set meets M2 by documented coverage or quality beyond what existed. Projections, hazard and scenarios are knowledge conditional on stated inputs. A correction, a replication or a negative result can meet M2 [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 4].

crit_W1.label: W1 follows from the evidence
crit_W1.def: The gain follows from data and analysis presented in this paper, not from assertion. A result the paper takes from a cited source is a dependency, not warrant for this paper's gain [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 5].

crit_W2.label: W2 uncertainty
crit_W2.def: Uncertainty is stated or bounded, or the gain is large compared with plausible error. A qualitative statement counts when the paper names the alternative interpretations it cannot exclude. For projections and hazard: stated epistemic and aleatory uncertainty (logic tree, ensemble) [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 5].

crit_W3.label: W3 principal threat checked
crit_W3.def: Name the most plausible alternative explanation or artifact for the gain first. Met when at least one reported check addresses that threat; checks of other things do not meet W3. Not applicable only for a data set release whose quality control is documented under W1 and W2. For projections and hazard: sensitivity to the dominant inputs, or retrospective or pseudo-prospective testing [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 5].

crit_W4.label: W4 internal consistency
crit_W4.def: No unresolved contradiction among the paper's own results, captions and claims bears on the gain [advance rubric 1.0.1, section 5].

hard_cases: S or I? Computing what a rival predicts is S. Fitting a model to data to estimate a quantity is I (fitting synthetic travel times to estimate a velocity is I). A model ensemble conditioned on observations to bound a quantity is I.

Premise or product? A check of a premise is V on the mode that owns it: methods for a computational method, instruments for an apparatus. A check of the product is V on the product's mode. E is only for establishing that a phenomenon is real; a check that a known measurement is not an artifact is V.

Conditions found in a live event (an eruption, an earthquake, a plume measured as it happens) are F on observation; past events known only from traces are F on reconstruction; conditions set in a laboratory are F on hypothesis.
A check reported only in the Methods or supplement goes right after the main-text step it supports, and its location says where it is.

Repeat means the same node as the step just before. Return after failure means the paper says an earlier attempt failed or was revised. Inherited is the authors' own earlier work, cited; cited is another group's result, used. In the final-paper sequence, code moves from the published text alone.

Locations: from the located text, cite the locator exactly as printed at the start of the paragraph (§3.2 ¶4) or the caption label as printed (Figure 3, Table 2). For a step read off a figure's content, add the PDF page when you have the PDF: Figure 3 (p. 5).
rating_notes: Frame: judge against what the field knew, could do and had available before submission (about 2021). Do not use later work, this paper's reception or its citations.

Judge the work, not the writing or the venue. Fluent claims of novelty, importance or a gap are not evidence; check the gap the introduction draws. The PDF shows the journal: prestige is not evidence.

Magnitude is the change from the starting state, not the result value: quantity, before -> after (units), against the scale it matters at (signal size, prior uncertainty, natural variability), then one sentence on why it matters. When no number applies, write 'not quantifiable:' and the reason: qualitative discrimination between rivals, first observation with no prior value, feasibility demonstration, or descriptive or taxonomic.
Advance score rates the gain the verdict rests on. Judge 4 and 5 by what the gain resolves or makes possible within the frame, not by predicted uptake.
'Local' means narrow in what can now be asserted, not small in geographic extent. A single-site study that settles a question for its subfield is a 3.
'Others will build on' is judged by how general the gain is, not by its type. A method or data set takes 4 only when its demonstrated improvement transfers beyond the test case.
Verdict and score agree: achieved takes 2 to 5, not demonstrated takes 1, unassessable takes no score. Novelty, warrant and impact stay separate: there is no weighted sum.

Novelty: score the highest anchor the result supports, not the approach. A known method in a new setting that finds a new phenomenon is a 3 or 4, not a 2. A bounded search rarely supports high confidence for 'apparently new component'.

Roles describe the kind of contribution, not its size, judged at publication. Transformative means the paper proposes and demonstrates a reframing; enabling means the new data, method or standard is demonstrated in the paper. Realized uptake is judged later, not here.
